findings.body: The mandatory master requires stage 1 to pin a 2,000-character question limit, one active run, five selection rounds, 20 conversations/account, 200/process, 40 sanitized turns, three retained result bundles, and 256 replay events. This shared limits contract exposes only drill/paging limits and the 60-minute idle limit, and its test blesses that incomplete shape. Later GRAPH/MEMORY/STREAM consumers would therefore have to invent unshared constants. Add the omitted literal limits to this contract (or another exported stage-1 contract) and test them here.
findings.title: Not done: Pin all stage-1 execution and memory-retention limits

findings.body: The 256-event requirement is a bounded retention window, not a maximum lifetime cursor value: the master explicitly says a cursor outside retained events requests an authorized refresh. Capping `sequence` at 255 makes the 257th event in a longer run invalid and prevents a rolling replay buffer from retaining later events with monotonic sequence numbers. Remove this upper bound, pin 256 as the retention capacity, and add a frame test using a sequence above 255.
findings.title: Not done: Keep event sequence valid beyond the 256-event replay window

findings.body: New evidence beyond the repaired reordered-selection path: `advertised.value` remains part of `scopeIdentity`, while `promisedHandles` is keyed only by handle. Thus two chart/table results with the same canonical selection, coordinate, and Actual kind but different values and different handles are accepted as separate scopes; even equal values with different handles prepare duplicate details. This permits contradictory displays for one Actual scope and does not enforce the required chart/table deduplication. Key the semantic scope without its value, then require its value and handle to agree.
findings.title: Treat one semantic Actual coordinate as one value and prepared handle

findings.body: This branch defines only the clarification presentation shape; it does not implement pending-request continuation, scope retention, capacity/expiry, authorization rechecks, cancellation, or restart outcomes required by done-when item 3. The approved task table assigns those behaviors and their end-to-end proofs to MEMORY, GRAPH, API, STREAM, CLIENT, and REGRESSION.
findings.title: Later: MEMORY/GRAPH/API/STREAM/CLIENT/REGRESSION must prove clarification lifecycle

findings.body: The ready/failed detail union is only the presentation contract. Scope preparation, deadlines, immutable source/mapping pins, stable full traversal, authorization rechecks, and browser identity/total comparisons required by done-when item 4 remain assigned to DRILL, PAGES, ANSWER, DETAIL, and BROWSER.
findings.title: Later: DRILL/PAGES/ANSWER/DETAIL/BROWSER must implement prepared Actual paging

findings.body: Pinning Anthropic and the model ID in capabilities does not establish direct ChatAnthropic execution, trusted instruction ordering, static-prefix caching, payload exclusions, typed vendor behavior, or gated live runs required by done-when item 6. Those implementations and proofs are assigned to MODEL, GRAPH, ANSWER, and LIVE.
findings.title: Later: MODEL/GRAPH/ANSWER/LIVE must prove Claude and static-cache boundaries
